findings.title: Members test no longer guards render order
findings.problem: In codemie-ui, the rewrite of ProjectMembersOrdering.test.tsx into ProjectMembersNoSortParams.test.tsx deletes the only assertion that the Members tab renders users in the order the server returns them (the old non-alphabetical Zed/Alice/bob fixture checked with renderedEmails()). The new test uses a single-user serverPage with user_count 1 and only checks that getUsers receives no sortBy/sortOrder. That cannot detect a reorder, and it never exercises the multi-page path.
findings.impact: After this change the Members tab is A to Z only because the backend default is A to Z and ProjectMembersManager does not reorder rows on the client (verified: no .sort/localeCompare/orderBy today). If a later change re-sorts, merges or filters pages on the client (for example on the budget-filter path), the tab silently loses A to Z order and no test fails. The guard the task asks for covers only half the contract.
findings.recommendation: Keep the new not.toHaveProperty('sortBy'/'sortOrder') assertions, and also restore a deliberately non-alphabetical multi-user serverPage (e.g. Zed, Alice, bob; set mockProject.user_count to match) with `await waitFor(() => expect(renderedEmails()).toEqual(serverEmailOrder))`, so the test fails if the Members tab ever reorders rows on the client, including on the budget-filter path.
